source_text: Βωμὸν γὰρ πρὸς τὴν τῶν δαιμόνων σπονδὴν ἀνακαύσαντες, ἱστᾶσι παρ' αὐτῷ ἀγαγόντες τὸν μάρτυρα, καὶ τῷ βωμῷ τὴν δεξιὰν ὑπτίαν ἐπαιωρῆσαι κελεύσαντες, ὡς χαλκῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ τῇ χειρὶ κατεχρήσαντο, λιβα νωτὸν αὐτῇ κακούργως ἐνθέντες φλεγόμενον. Ἤλπιζον γὰρ τῇ τοῦ πυρὸς βίᾳ τὴν χεῖρα καταπαλαισθεῖσαν, ἀνάγκῃ τῷ βωμῷ ταχέως λιβανωτὸν ἐπαφή σειν. Φεῦ τῆς πολυπλόκου τῶν ἀσεβῶν μαγγανείας! Ἐπειδὴ μυρίοις, φησὶ, τὴν γνώμην οὐκ ἐκάμψαμεν τραύμασι, κάμψωμεν ἐν φλογὶ τοῦ φιλονείκου παλαιστοῦ κἂν τὴν χεῖρα. Ἐπειδὴ ποικίλαις μηχα ναῖς τὴν ψυχὴν οὐκ ἐσείσαμεν, τὴν δεξιὰν γοῦν πυρὶ προσαγαγόντες σαλεύσωμεν. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ταύτης οἱ δείλαιοι τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀπώναντο. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ φλὸξ τὴν χεῖρα διέτρωγεν· ἔμενε δὲ ἡ χεὶρ, ὡς τέφραν τὴν φλόγα βαστάζουσα. Οὐκ ἔδωκε τῷ πολεμοῦντι πυρὶ κατὰ τοὺς φυγάδας τὰ νῶτα, ἀλλὰ ἄτρεπτος εἱστήκει κατὰ φλογὸς ἀριστεύουσα, καὶ τὰς τοῦ Προφήτου λέγειν τῷ μάρτυρι διδοῦσα φω νάς· Εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ὁ Θεός μου, ὁ διδάσκων τὰς χεῖράς μου εἰς παράταξιν, καὶ τοὺς δακτύ λους μου εἰς πόλεμον. Πῦρ γὰρ χειρὶ συνεπλέκετο, καὶ τοῦ πυρὸς τὰ τῆς ἥττης εὑρίσκετο. Φλογὶ καὶ μάρτυρος δεξιᾷ συνεκροτεῖτο πάλη, ἀλλ' ἦν τῆς δεξιᾶς καινή τις τῶν παλαισμάτων ἡ νίκη, τῆς μὲν φλογὸς διὰ μέσου τῆς χειρὸς ἐκπιπτούσης, τῆς χειρὸς δὲ ἔτι τεταμένης πρὸς πάλην. Ὢ χειρὸς φιλονεικοτέρας πυρός! ὢ χειρὸς, κάμπτεσθαι πυρὶ μὴ μαθούσης! ὢ πυρὸς, ἡττᾶσθαι χειρὶ διδαχθέντος! Σίδηρος τῇ τοῦ πυρὸς εἴκει τυραννίδι χαυνούμενος· χαλκὸς τῇ τοῦ πυρὸς παραχωρεῖ δυναστείᾳ· οἶδε τούτῳ καὶ λίθων ἀντιτυπία νικᾶσθαι. Ἀλλ' ὁ πάντα τοῦ πυρὸς βιαζόμενος τόνος μάρτυρος τὴν δεξιὰν τεταμένην οὐκ ἔκαμψε κατακαίων. Εἰκότως ἂν ὁ μάρτυς ἐπὶ τούτῳ πρὸς τὸν Δεσπότην βοήσειεν· Ἐκράτησας τῆς χειρὸς τῆς δεξιᾶς μου, καὶ ἐν τῇ βουλῇ σου ὡδήγησάς με, καὶ μετὰ δόξης προσελάβου με. Τί σε, ὦ γενναῖε τοῦ Χριστοῦ στρατιῶτα, προσείπω; Ἀνδριάντα καλέσω; Πολύ σε τῆς καρτερίας ἠλάττωσα. Τὸν μὲν γὰρ πῦρ μαλάττει δεξάμενον· σοῦ δὲ τὴν δεξιὰν ὀφθῆναι μόνον κινουμένην οὐκ ἔπεισεν. Ἂν σιδηροῦν ὀνομάσω, καὶ τὴν τοιαύτην τῆς σῆς ἀνδρίας εὑρίσκω λειπομένην εἰκόνα. Σὺ γὰρ μόνος ἔπεισας φλόγα μὴ βιάζεσθαι χεῖρα· σὺ μόνος ἐκτήσω θυσιαστήριον δεξιάν· σὺ μόνος δεξιᾷ φλεγομένῃ τὰ τῶν δαιμόνων ἐῤῥάπισας πρόσωπα, καὶ τότε μὲν ἀπηνθρακωμένῃ χειρὶ τὰς ἐκείνων κεφαλὰς συγκατέτηξας· νῦν δὲ τεφρωθείσῃ ταύτῃ τὰς αὐτῶν στρατιὰς ἀποτυφλοῖς καταπατῶν. Ἀλλὰ τί παιδικοῖς ἐλαττῶ τὸν ἀριστέα ψελλίσμασι; Ταῖς μεγαλοπρεπεστέραις τοίνυν τὸν εἰς αὐτὸν ὕμνον παραχωρήσωμεν γλώτταις· τὰς μεγαλοφωνοτέρας τῶν διδασκάλων ἐπ' αὐτῷ καλέσωμεν σάλπιγγας. Ἀνάστητέ μοι νῦν, ὦ λαμπροὶ τῶν ἀθλητικῶν κατορθωμάτων ζωγράφοι· τὴν τοῦ στρατηγοῦ κολοβωθεῖσαν εἰκόνα ταῖς ὑμετέραις μεγαλύνατε τέχναις. Ἀμαυρότερον παρ' ἐμοῦ τὸν στεφανίτην γραφέντα τοῖς τῆς ὑμετέρας σοφίας περιλάμψατε χρώμασιν. Ἀπέλθω τῇ τῶν ἀριστευμάτων τοῦ μάρτυρος παρ' ὑμῶν νενικημένος γραφῇ· χαίρω τὴν τοιαύτην τῆς ὑμετέρας ἰσχύος σήμερον νίκην ἡττώμενος. Ἴδω τῆς χειρὸς πρὸς τὸ πῦρ ἀκριβέστερον παρ' ὑμῶν γραφομένην τὴν πάλην· ἴδω φαιδρότερον ἐπὶ τῆς ὑμετέρας τὸν παλαιστὴν γεγραμμένον εἰκόνος. Κλαυσάτωσαν δαίμονες, καὶ νῦν ταῖς τοῦ μάρτυρος ἐν ὑμῖν ἀριστείαις πληττόμενοι. Φλεγομένη πάλιν αὐτοῖς ἡ χεὶρ καὶ νικῶσα δεικνύσθω. Ἐγγραφέσθω τῷ πίνακι καὶ ὁ τῶν παλαισμάτων ἀγωνοθέτης Χριστός· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The hand as altar and the fire's defeat
orientation: Basil is describing the climax of Barlaam's martyrdom: the persecutors place burning incense in his outstretched right hand over a lit altar, hoping the fire will force him to drop it, but the hand remains unconquered.
pass_a_gloss: For having kindled an altar for the libation to the demons, they stand the martyr beside it, having brought him, and having ordered his right hand to be raised stretched out over the altar, they used the hand as a bronze altar, having wickedly placed in it burning incense. For they hoped that the hand, having been wrestled down by the force of the fire, would by necessity quickly bring the incense into contact with the altar. Alas for the many-wiled trickery of the impious! Since, he says, we did not bend his purpose with ten thousand wounds, let us bend at least the hand of the contentious wrestler in flame. Since with varied devices we did not shake his soul, let us at least, having brought his right hand to the fire, shake it. But not even of this hope did the wretches enjoy the fruit. For the flame was eating through the hand; but the hand remained, as though carrying the flame as ash. It did not give its back to the warring fire like the fugitives, but stood unshaken, excelling against the flame, and giving the martyr the words of the Prophet to speak: Blessed is the Lord my God, who teaches my hands for battle array, and my fingers for war. For fire was grappling with a hand, and the marks of defeat were found to belong to the fire. A wrestling match was being joined between flame and the martyr's right hand, but the victory of the wrestling moves was some new one belonging to the right hand, the flame falling out through the middle of the hand, and the hand still stretched out for the wrestling. O hand more contentious than fire! O hand that did not learn to be bent by fire! O fire that was taught to be defeated by a hand! Iron yields to the tyranny of fire, being softened; bronze gives way to the power of fire; the resistance of stones knows itself to be conquered by it. But the force of fire that overpowers all things did not bend the martyr's right hand, stretched out, while burning it. Reasonably would the martyr cry out to the Master over this: You held my right hand, and in your counsel you guided me, and with glory you received me. What shall I call you, O noble soldier of Christ? Shall I call you a statue? I have greatly diminished your endurance. For fire softens a statue when it receives it; but it did not persuade your right hand to be seen moved even once. If I name you iron, I find even such an image of your courage lacking. For you alone persuaded flame not to force a hand; you alone acquired a right hand as an altar; you alone with a burning right hand slapped the faces of the demons, and then with a charred hand you melted down their heads; now with this hand turned to ash you blind their armies, trampling them. But why do I diminish the champion with childish stammerings? Let us then yield the hymn to him to more magnificent tongues; let us summon the louder trumpets of the teachers for him. Rise up for me now, O brilliant painters of athletic achievements; magnify with your arts the mutilated image of the commander. Illuminate with the colors of your wisdom the crown-winner who has been painted too dimly by me. May I depart defeated by your painting of the martyr's feats; I rejoice today in being defeated by such a victory of your strength. May I see the wrestling of the hand against the fire painted by you more accurately; may I see the wrestler drawn more radiantly on your image. Let the demons weep, even now being struck by the martyr's feats in you. Let the hand be shown again burning and conquering them. Let Christ, the president of the wrestling matches, be inscribed on the tablet too; to whom be glory to the ages of ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: to enjoy the fruit of, profit from
to grapple with, be intertwined in combat

choices.term: ὡς χαλκῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ τῇ χειρὶ κατεχρήσαντο
choices.english: they used the hand as a bronze altar
choices.why: κατεχρήσαντο takes the dative χειρί as its object and the dative θυσιαστηρίῳ as predicate; the hand itself functions as the altar
rejected: they treated the hand as if to a bronze altar
they made use of the hand for a bronze altar

choices.term: τὸν μὲν γὰρ πῦρ μαλάττει δεξάμενον
choices.english: for fire softens a statue when it receives it
choices.why: πῦρ is the subject of μαλάττει, and δεξάμενον (the statue) is the object; the statue receives the fire and is softened by it
rejected: a statue, receiving fire, is softened by it
fire, receiving a statue, softens it

choices.why: the verb means to melt down or fuse by heat; the heads are the object, not 'together' with anything else

choices.english: the president of the wrestling matches
choices.why: παλαισμάτων specifically means wrestling moves or matches, so the ἀγωνοθέτης presides over the wrestling contest, not a general contest

choices.term: ἀπέλθω τῇ τῶν ἀριστευμάτων τοῦ μάρτυρος παρ' ὑμῶν νενικημένος γραφῇ
choices.english: May I depart defeated by your painting of the martyr's feats
choices.why: νενικημένος is passive ('having been defeated') and γραφῇ is the dative of means; Basil wishes to be outdone by the painters' depiction
rejected: May I depart having defeated your painting of the martyr's feats
May I go away conquered by the martyr's feats from you

choices.english: Let him be inscribed on the tablet
choices.why: ἐγγραφέσθω is a third-person imperative passive ('let him be inscribed'), and πίνακι is the dative of place where
rejected: Let him write on the tablet

pass_b_english: They lit an altar for a drink offering to the demons, brought the martyr and stood him beside it, and ordered him to stretch his right hand out over the altar with the palm turned upward. They used the hand as a bronze altar, wickedly placing burning incense in it. For they hoped that the hand would be wrestled down by the force of the fire and would quickly be compelled to drop the incense onto the altar. What a tangled trick of the impious! “Since,” they say, “we have not bent his resolve with countless wounds, let us at least bend the hand of this stubborn wrestler in the fire. Since we have not shaken his soul with various devices, let us at least bring his right hand to the fire and make it waver.” But the wretches did not profit even from this hope. The fire gnawed through the hand, but the hand remained, bearing the flame as though it were ash. It did not turn its back to the attacking fire like a deserter, but stood unshaken, proving itself best against the fire, and giving the martyr the words of the Prophet to speak: “Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war” (Psalm 18:34; Psalm 17:35 LXX). Fire grappled with a hand, and the fire was found to bear the marks of defeat. A wrestling match was joined between the fire and the martyr’s right hand, but the victory of the right hand’s wrestling moves was something new: the fire fell through the middle of the hand, while the hand remained stretched out for the contest. O hand more stubborn than fire! O hand that never learned to bend to fire! O fire that was taught to be defeated by a hand! Iron yields to the tyranny of fire and is softened. Bronze gives way to the power of fire. Even the resistance of stones, as we know, is overcome by it. But the force of fire that overpowers everything did not bend the martyr’s stretched-out right hand, even as it burned it. Fittingly the martyr might cry out to the Master: “You held my right hand, and in your counsel you guided me, and with glory you received me” (Psalm 73:24; Psalm 72:24 LXX). What shall I call you, noble soldier of Christ? Shall I call you a statue? I fall far short of your endurance. For fire, receiving it, softens a statue, but it could not make your right hand appear to move. If I call you iron, I find that even this image falls short of your courage. For you alone persuaded the fire not to force a hand. You alone made your right hand an altar. You alone with a burning right hand struck the faces of the demons, and then with a charred hand you melted their heads along with it; now with that hand burned to ashes you blind their armies as you trample them. But why do I diminish the champion with childish stammering? Let us yield the hymn in his honor to more magnificent tongues. Let us summon the louder trumpets of the teachers for him. Rise up now for me, brilliant painters of athletic achievements. Magnify with your arts the mutilated image of the commander. Illuminate with the colors of your wisdom the crowned victor whom I have painted too dimly. May I depart defeated by your painting of the martyr’s feats. I rejoice today to be defeated by such a victory of your strength. Let me see the wrestling match of the hand against the fire painted by you more accurately. Let me see the wrestler drawn more brightly on your image. Let the demons weep, struck now too by the martyr’s feats in your work. Let the burning hand be shown again to them, victorious. Let Christ also, the umpire of the wrestling matches, be inscribed on the tablet—to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: holding the fire as though it were ashes
problems.why: Greek says hand held flame *as ashes*, not held fire as if it were ashes; simile of weight/ease, not identity
problems.fix: bearing the flame as though it were ash

problems.quote: it could not persuade your right hand to move even when it was seen
problems.source_quote: σοῦ δὲ τὴν δεξιὰν ὀφθῆναι μόνον κινουμένην οὐκ ἔπεισεν
problems.why: Greek says fire could not persuade your right hand *to appear* moving, i.e., to seem to move/relent
problems.fix: it could not make your right hand appear to move

problems.quote: and the defeat belonged to the fire.
problems.source_quote: καὶ τοῦ πυρὸς τὰ τῆς ἥττης εὑρίσκετο.
problems.why: Source says 'the tokens of defeat were found on the fire' (fire was defeated); English says defeat 'belonged to' fire, which is ambiguous.
problems.fix: and the fire was found to bear the marks of defeat.
problems.ruling: τα τῆς ἥττης = 'tokens/signs of defeat'; 'defeat belonged to' obscures that fire bore the marks.

edits.old: holding the fire as though it were ashes
edits.new: bearing the flame as though it were ash

edits.old: it could not persuade your right hand to move even when it was seen
edits.new: it could not make your right hand appear to move

edits.old: and the defeat belonged to the fire
edits.new: and the fire was found to bear the marks of defeat

fixed: Changed 'holding the fire as though it were ashes' to 'bearing the flame as though it were ash' to match the source's simile of weight/ease (ὡς τέφραν τὴν φλόγα βαστάζουσα).
Changed 'it could not persuade your right hand to move even when it was seen' to 'it could not make your right hand appear to move' to match the source's ὀφθῆναι μόνον κινουμένην (to appear moving).
Changed 'and the defeat belonged to the fire' to 'and the fire was found to bear the marks of defeat' to match the source's τὰ τῆς ἥττης εὑρίσκετο (the tokens of defeat were found on the fire).

problems.why: ὑπτίαν means 'with palm down/flat,' not 'upward'; the hand was held flat over the altar, palm downward.

problems.quote: with that hand reduced to ashes
problems.why: τεφρωθείσῃ is passive participle, 'having been reduced to ashes' (by the fire), not merely 'reduced to ashes' as a state; the hand was actively burned to ash.
problems.fix: with that hand burned to ashes

problems.quote: For fire softens a statue when it receives it
problems.source_quote: Τὸν μὲν γὰρ πῦρ μαλάττει δεξάμενον
problems.why: Source says fire softens 'him' (the statue, acc.), not 'when it receives it.' The fire receives and softens the statue.
problems.fix: For fire, receiving it, softens a statue
problems.ruling: δεξάμενον modifies τὸν (statue), accusative: 'having received him.' English inverts agent/patient.

problems.quote: Let the burning hand be shown again defeating them
problems.source_quote: Φλεγομένη πάλιν αὐτοῖς ἡ χεὶρ καὶ νικῶσα δεικνύσθω
problems.why: πάλιν modifies 'δεικνύσθω' ('be shown again'), not 'νικῶσα.' English reads 'again defeating' rather than 'shown again, defeating.'
problems.fix: Let the burning hand be shown again to them, and defeating
problems.ruling: πάλιν modifies δεικνύσθω, not νικῶσα: 'be shown again, defeating' ≠ 'again defeating.' Misplaced modifier.

problems.quote: Let Christ, the president of the wrestling matches, be inscribed on the tablet
problems.source_quote: Ἐγγραφέσθω τῷ πίνακι καὶ ὁ τῶν παλαισμάτων ἀγωνοθέτης Χριστός
problems.why: ἀγωνοθέτης = 'umpire/judge of the contest,' not 'president.' Also 'καὶ' ('also/even') before Christ is omitted.
problems.fix: Let Christ also, the umpire of the wrestling matches, be inscribed on the tablet
problems.ruling: ἀγωνοθέτης = 'umpire/judge,' not 'president'; καὶ = 'also' before Christ is omitted, changing emphasis.

problems.source_quote: Ἐκράτησας τῆς χειρὸς τῆς δεξιᾶς μου, καὶ ἐν τῇ βουλῇ σου ὡδήγησάς με, καὶ μετὰ δόξης προσελάβου με
problems.why: The citation should be Psalm 73:24 (72:24 LXX) per brief, but the English adds v.23 which is not quoted; the source only quotes v.24.
problems.ruling: Source quotes only Psalm 72:24 LXX (Ἐκράτησας...προσελάβου με); English cites v.23-24, adding v.23 not in the text.

problems.quote: with a charred hand you melted down their heads
problems.source_quote: ἀπηνθρακωμένῃ χειρὶ τὰς ἐκείνων κεφαλὰς συγκατέτηξας
problems.why: συγκατέτηξας means 'melted down together with,' implying the hand was also being consumed; 'melted down their heads' loses the reciprocal destruction.
problems.fix: with a charred hand you melted their heads along with it
problems.ruling: συγκατέτηξας means 'melted down together with'; English 'melted down their heads' loses the prefix συν- indicating joint destruction.

τεφρωθείσῃ is passive participle, 'having been reduced to ashes'; changed to 'burned to ashes'.
Τὸν μὲν γὰρ πῦρ μαλάττει δεξάμενον: fire receives and softens the statue; changed to 'For fire, receiving it, softens a statue'.
πάλιν modifies δεικνύσθω ('be shown again'), not νικῶσα; changed to 'be shown again to them, and defeating'.

ἀγωνοθέτης = 'umpire/judge of the contest,' not 'president'; also καὶ ('also/even') before Christ omitted; changed to 'Let Christ also, the umpire of the wrestling matches, be inscribed on the tablet'.
The source only quotes Psalm 73:24 (72:24 LXX), not v.23; changed citation to 'Psalm 73:24; Psalm 72:24 LXX'.
συγκατέτηξας means 'melted down together with,' implying the hand was also being consumed; changed to 'melted their heads along with it'.

problems.why: ὑπτίαν means 'palm upward,' not 'palm held flat'; the hand is upturned to receive incense.

problems.quote: I would greatly diminish your endurance
problems.why: Source means 'I fall far short of your endurance' (I am much less than your endurance), not 'I diminish your endurance.'
problems.fix: I fall far short of your endurance
problems.ruling: ἠλάττωσα is 1st person 'I lessened/fell short'; 'I diminish your endurance' misattributes agency to the martyr's endurance rather than the speaker's inadequacy.

problems.quote: the burning hand be shown again to them, and defeating
problems.source_quote: φλεγομένη πάλιν αὐτοῖς ἡ χεὶρ καὶ νικῶσα δεικνύσθω
problems.why: δεικνύσθω is passive 'let it be shown,' but 'defeating' lacks an object—'and conquering' or 'victorious' would be clearer.
problems.fix: let the burning hand be shown again to them, victorious
problems.ruling: 'and defeating' is ungrammatical English; νικῶσα needs 'victorious' or 'conquering' to form a proper clause.

edits.old: I would greatly diminish your endurance
edits.new: I fall far short of your endurance

edits.old: Let the burning hand be shown again to them, and defeating
edits.new: Let the burning hand be shown again to them, victorious

fixed: ὑπτίαν means 'palm upward,' not 'palm held flat'; the hand is upturned to receive incense.
Πολύ σε τῆς καρτερίας ἠλάττωσα means 'I fall far short of your endurance,' not 'I diminish your endurance.'
δεικνύσθω is passive 'let it be shown,' and 'defeating' lacks an object; 'victorious' is clearer.

dismissed.why: ὑπτίαν means 'palm upward' but also 'supine, laid back'—the hand is stretched out flat/backward over the altar, not just palm-up; 'turned upward' slightly misrepresents the posture of the hand stretched out over the altar
dismissed.note: ὑπτίαν here means palm upward, which fits a hand holding incense, so 'with the palm turned upward' is correct.

dismissed.quote: with a charred hand you melted their heads along with it
dismissed.why: συγκατέτηξας means 'melted down together', but 'along with it' is vague; the hand was charred/coal-like (ἀπηνθρακωμένῃ) and melted their heads along with (the hand itself being the instrument)
dismissed.note: The proposed fix is identical to the current English, and the rendering is fine.

dismissed.quote: now with that hand burned to ashes you blind their armies
dismissed.why: τεφρωθείσῃ is dative 'to/with the hand that has been reduced to ashes', but the present ἀποτυφλοῖς shows ongoing action; 'burned to ashes' suggests completion, but the hand is still active now
dismissed.note: τεφρωθείσῃ describes a hand already reduced to ash that still acts now; 'burned to ashes' is accurate.

dismissed.quote: bearing the flame as though it were ash
dismissed.why: The hand bore the flame *as if the flame were ash* (i.e., effortlessly), not 'as though it were ash' referring to the hand; the simile compares flame to ash, not hand to ash
dismissed.note: In the English, 'it' naturally refers to the flame, which matches the Greek simile.

dismissed.quote: You alone made your right hand an altar
dismissed.why: ἐκτήσω means 'acquired, obtained, won' (aorist of κτάομαι), not 'made'; the martyr won/possessed his right hand as an altar—an active achievement, not fabrication
dismissed.note: 'Made your right hand an altar' is a fair idiomatic rendering of ἐκτήσω θυσιαστήριον δεξιάν; 'won your right hand as an altar' is stilted.
